correctness.rationale: Conditional on every other internal vertex, g:{0,1}^2->{0,1} is monotone and delta=g11-g10-g01+g00. Setting protected reliabilities from p to one yields I=(1-p)^2 E[delta]. With <=5 total vertices only one other internal variable w exists; sign change requires delta0,delta1 of opposite signs. Monotonicity excludes delta0=-1,delta1=+1; the reverse forces majority-of-three Boolean viability. All three pairs of internal vertices must then each form an s-to-t directed path and each must meet disjoint L={s-out-neighbors} and R={t-in-neighbors}, impossible on a triangle. The explicit six-vertex DAG edges 01,03,12,14,25,34,45 have Boolean reachability x1*x2 + x1*x4 + x3*x4 in OR form and delta=(1,0,0,-1) on remaining pair, giving I=(1-p)^2(1-2p). Independently enumerated 2^15=32768 forward-labelled DAGs times 6 pairs=196608 exact profiles using a separate reachability bitset code: 18 coefficient triples, precisely 24 strict sign reversals, all (1,0,-1). No cyclic six-node classification is claimed. Check includes exact vertex extrema for quadratic in [0,1], not just sampled p.

value.rationale: A sharp realizability obstruction for a natural intervention interaction, together with a first possible six-node witness and exhaustive six-node DAG polynomial classification, is a motivated structural benchmark for directed reachability reliability. The exact threshold distinguishes general Boolean importance from graph-implementable importance; nontrivial even at six vertices, not an arbitrary tiny slice.

limitations: Six-node switching profile covers DAGs only. Five-node impossibility covers directed cycles.
Perfect vertex protection, independent Bernoulli survival, fixed links; no ecological intervention efficacy claim.
